question: Recently, Iranian authorities have intensified the unlawful confiscation of assets belonging to Baha’is. These actions form part of a four-decade pattern of state-sponsored expropriations since the Islamic Revolution.

Since then, authorities have seized holy sites, cemeteries, homes and businesses, and frozen bank accounts, leading to the dismantling of families’ lives and depriving them of their livelihoods, education and medical care. Such measures, purportedly justified under Article 49 of the Iranian Constitution, represent a flagrant misuse of law.

A judge of the Special Court for Article 49 in Isfahan reportedly declared his intent to ‘ruin the lives’ of Baha’is and to ‘strip all Baha’is of Isfahan of their belongings.’ These expropriated assets are funneled into the Execution of Imam Khomeini’s Order (EIKO), a powerful, state-linked conglomerate operating under the direct authority of the Iranian Supreme Leader.

EIKO has been instrumental in the economic strangulation and impoverishment of Baha’is, long profiting from assets expropriated from members of this peaceful religious community. Given these developments 1.
What concrete measures will the EU pursue to hold EIKO and the Iranian authorities accountable for the ongoing, unlawful dispossession of the livelihoods of Bahá’is?
What immediate action will the Vice-President / High Representative take to prevent the economic strangulation of Baha’is in Iran?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (5.1.2026) The EU monitors very closely the situation of ethnic and religious minorities in Iran, including the Baha’is, as part of its overall commitment to the human rights situation in the country.

The EU is using every opportunity, both privately and publicly1, including within United Nations (UN) fora2, to urge the Iranian authorities to ensure respect for the fundamental freedoms of all Iranian people and to uphold their obligations under the international law, particularly under the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights and the Convention on the Rights of the Child, to both of which Iran is a party.

In this context, the EU is a strong supporter of the UN accountability mechanisms. Since 2011, the EU has in place restrictive measures related to serious human rights violations, which have been substantially expanded in recent years in Iran. The latest measures for serious human rights violations in the country were adopted in April 20253, and this approach will continue as long as necessary.
